Peter / Security team —

Thanks again for coordinating the sealed-bundle update window next week. I wanted to share the proposed depot ingestion + operator handback protocol for your review so we can lock the courier arrival window and the operator overlap. Main points below:

- Delivery window: Tue 30 Jun, 09:00–11:00 PT. Courier will present sealed transport case to FortessHealth depot gate.
- Parties on site: FortessHealth operator (named below), Redwood operator (remote oversight — we will not bring hardware on-site).
- Acceptance checks: manifest match, tamper-evidence inspection, signature verification on signed_image_v1.2.tar.sig, and HSM-wrapped key confirmation.
- Operator handback: After ingest validation and break-glass verification (test vector signature check), operator signs the custody receipt (courier_manifest_20260630.csv).

Attachments: depot_ingest_checklist_v3.pdf (checklist we use for site intake), signed_image_v1.2.tar.sig (signature blob for the release). Please review the checklist and confirm the courier details and the FortessHealth operator contact.

Open items for your answers:
1) Will your on-site operator perform a secondary identity check (photo ID + operator badge)?
2) Do you require us to run a sample signature verification on-site, or will you perform verification and send a signed acceptance?
3) Any specific parking/entrance instructions we should relay to the courier?

If everything looks good we will pre-stage the DocuSign custody envelope and courier manifest — I can circulate the envelope link once you confirm the operator contact.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Field Operations

Peter —

Thanks for the quick reply and the operator contact. A few technical clarifications to make on-site verification straightforward:

1) Signature format: the release bundle is signed with a Redwood release key (RSA-4096) and we are sharing a detached signature file (signed_image_v1.2.tar.sig). We will provide the public key as PEM and include the SHA256 fingerprint for your verification.

Public key fingerprint (SHA256): 3f:9b:12:5a:8d:3c:77:9b:ae:48:2f:1d:6a:2e:47:8c:bb:9d:4e:1f:7a:6c:31:44:5b:ee:2a:9d:9c:80:11:55

2) Minimal verification steps (command line):
- Verify tar integrity: tar -tvf signed_image_v1.2.tar.gz | head -n 20
- Check signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood_release_pub.pem -signature signed_image_v1.2.tar.sig signed_image_v1.2.tar.gz

If the command outputs "Verified OK" then the payload is intact and signed by our release key. We will place redwood_release_pub.pem in the Drive folder linked below (read-only).

3) HSM-wrapped key: the operator will receive a manifest entry stating the KMS key ID used to wrap the symmetric key used for the image encrypt/decrypt. The KMS ID is inert for on-site verification but required for audit trails.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-depot-ingest-checks (redwood_release_pub.pem and checklist live here).

We can also remote into a console if you prefer a guided verification (we use an ephemeral session token and logs that we will share post-check).

Jonas Weber
Release Engineering — Redwood Inference
